title: IPC admin.peers.list result
description: One page of the dial gate's state per allowlisted peer (2.2, CONNECTIVITY.md §19): ascending by canonical string, at most 512 rows a page (a row is up to 194 bytes with the three original fields and about 220 with `route_held_until` — 512 of them about 110 KB against the 128 KiB body, 1024 would overflow it; architect-cto's ruling of 2026-10-07, re-read 2026-10-21), `next` the last row's peer when more remain and absent on the last page. Never an address: what holds a peer is read as times and a bounded class. `route_held_until` is served on a connection that negotiated 2.6 or later; below 2.6 the 2.2 row -- 1.0.0's shape, without it -- is served unchanged (1.1.0 widens behind the minor under ADR-0017 A 2026-10-07: a closed result shape widens behind a new minor while the old shape is served below it, a 2.2 client refusing an unknown member).

backoff_until.description: Dials to the peer are refused until then, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; absent when no backoff runs.

quarantined_until.description: Every known address of the peer is quarantined until then, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch: the earliest release among them, the moment the peer is dialable again. Absent while any known address is dialable, since quarantine is per address and a peer with a good route is not held by it (CONNECTIVITY.md section 19).

route_held_until.description: The peer's circuit routes are held until then, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch: the latest hold among them, each a `/p2p-circuit` route whose dial failed at its relay hop (ADR-0011 A 2026-10-21, CONNECTIVITY.md section 12). Absent when no route is held, and never present below IPC 2.6, the minor that brings it. A hold is per route and never backs the peer off: a peer with a direct route stays dialable over it while this is set, which is why the field stands apart from `quarantined_until` and `backoff_until` rather than folding into either.

last_outcome.description: How the last dial to, or connection with, the peer ended; absent until the first since the daemon started. Every refusal folds to `denied` — a route hold's included, which is why `route_held_until` is read beside it; the connectivity log line names the finer class.

peers.description: Unique by peer and strictly ascending; JSON Schema cannot state the order, the Rust mirror refuses a page that breaks it.
